question: If 7 N force is applied on a brick and it moves through 5 m, then what will be the work done?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 35 J.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Work done (W) = Force (F) × Displacement (s) in the direction of the force. (कार्य = बल × विस्थापन)

◦ Here, F = 7 N and s = 5 m.

◦ W = 7 × 5 = 35 joule (J).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of work (and energy) is the joule (J); 1 J = 1 N × 1 m.

• The CGS unit of work is the erg; 1 joule = 10⁷ erg. Hence "35 Erg" (Option 4) is a completely different, far smaller quantity.

• Work is a scalar quantity, although both force and displacement are vectors.

NOTE

• General formula: W = F s cos θ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.

◦ If θ = 0° → maximum positive work; if θ = 90° → zero work (e.g., a coolie carrying a load on his head walking horizontally); if θ = 180° → negative work (e.g., friction).

• The joule is named after the English physicist James Prescott Joule.

question: ________________is celebrated in Jharkhand immediately after Diwali on the new moon day in the honour of cattle.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sohrai.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sohrai" is a famous harvest and cattle festival of Jharkhand celebrated immediately after Diwali, on the new moon day (Amavasya), in honour of cattle. (सोहराई पर्व — झारखंड)

◦ Villagers bathe, decorate and worship their cows and bullocks, and the walls of homes are painted with the celebrated Sohrai wall art, which has a GI tag (Sohrai Khovar painting, Hazaribagh).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bhagta Parab is another Jharkhand festival (Chaitra–Vaisakh) marking the transition of spring to summer, associated with the Chhau dance and the worship of Budha Baba.

• Rohini is a Jharkhand festival marking the start of the sowing of seeds.

• Makar (Tusu Parab) is celebrated at Makar Sankranti in January.

NOTE

• Other major festivals of Jharkhand: Sarhul (worship of the Sal tree by tribal communities), Karma, Jani Shikar and Tusu.

• Jharkhand was carved out of Bihar on 15 November 2000 (birth anniversary of Birsa Munda); its capital is Ranchi.

question: Which of the following novels is NOT written by Mulk Raj Anand?
option_3: Private Life of an Indian Prince
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Guide.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "The Guide" (1958) was written by R. K. Narayan, not by Mulk Raj Anand. (द गाइड — आर. के. नारायण)

◦ It won R. K. Narayan the Sahitya Akademi Award (1960) and was made into the famous Hindi film *Guide* (1965) starring Dev Anand.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mulk Raj Anand (1905–2004) was a pioneer of Indian writing in English and a champion of the oppressed. His major works include:

◦ Untouchable (1935), Coolie (1936), Two Leaves and a Bud (1937), The Village, Across the Black Waters, The Sword and the Sickle (1942), The Big Heart and Private Life of an Indian Prince (1953).

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan and the Sahitya Akademi Award for *Morning Face*.

NOTE

• R. K. Narayan created the fictional town of Malgudi; his works include *Swami and Friends*, *The Bachelor of Arts*, *The English Teacher*, *The Financial Expert*, *The Man-Eater of Malgudi* and *Malgudi Days*.

• The "Big Three" of early Indian English fiction: Mulk Raj Anand, R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao.

question: Which of the dance was immediately preceded by a practice session called sevakali and undertaken in the precincts of a temple?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathakali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kathakali, the classical dance-drama of Kerala, was traditionally preceded by a practice/ritual session known as "sevakali", performed within the precincts of a temple. (कथकली — केरल)

◦ Kathakali is famous for its elaborate make-up (chutti), huge headgear, billowing costumes and stylised eye and facial expressions; themes are drawn mainly from the Ramayana and Mahabharata.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Kathak — classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh), noted for footwork (tatkar), pirouettes (chakkars) and gharanas like Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.

• Odissi — classical dance of Odisha, characterised by the tribhanga posture; linked to the Jagannath temple and the Maharis.

• Kuchipudi — classical dance-drama of Andhra Pradesh, known for the *tarangam* (dancing on the rim of a brass plate).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (UP), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• All are governed by the Natya Shastra attributed to Bharat Muni.

question: Which of the following is a duty of the Attorney General of India?
option_1: To give advice to the Government of India on legal matters
option_2: To act as a judge in the Supreme Court
option_4: To represent India in international bodies
solution_text:
The correct answer is To give advice to the Government of India on legal matters.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Attorney General of India (AGI) is the highest law officer of the country, appointed by the President under Article 76 of the Constitution. (भारत के महान्यायवादी — अनुच्छेद 76)

◦ His primary duty is to give advice to the Government of India upon such legal matters as are referred to him by the President, and to perform other duties of a legal character assigned to him.

◦ He also appears on behalf of the Government of India in all cases in the Supreme Court and in any High Court in which the Government of India is concerned.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Qualification: the AGI must be qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court, but he does not act as a judge (so Option 2 is wrong).

• The Advocate General (Article 165) advises the State Government (so Option 3 is wrong); representing India in international bodies is the work of diplomats/ambassadors (so Option 4 is wrong).

• The AGI has the right of audience in all courts of India and can take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament and their committees, but cannot vote (Article 88).

• He holds office during the pleasure of the President; there is no fixed tenure and no prescribed removal procedure.

NOTE

• India's first Attorney General was M. C. Setalvad (the longest-serving too).

• Other law officers: Solicitor General of India and Additional Solicitors General (these are statutory, not constitutional, posts).

question: The cultural heritage of Siddhis from _________ dates back to almost 300 years and their Siddhi Dhamal dance is an exquisite art form.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gujarat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Siddis (Siddhis) of Gujarat are a community of African (Bantu) descent whose cultural heritage in the region goes back nearly 300 years, and their vigorous Siddhi Dhamal (Dhamaal) dance is a celebrated folk art form. (सिद्दी धमाल — गुजरात)

◦ The dance is performed with drums (dhol, mugarman), coconut-shell rattles (mai misra) and peacock-feather ornaments, usually at weddings and festivals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Siddi communities are also found in Karnataka, Maharashtra and parts of Andhra Pradesh; in Gujarat they are concentrated around Junagadh, Gir Somnath and Jamnagar.

• They are recognised as a Scheduled Tribe in Gujarat, Karnataka and the Union Territory of Daman & Diu.

• Their ancestors came to India as sailors, soldiers, merchants and slaves with Arab and Portuguese traders; Malik Ambar of Ahmadnagar was a famous Siddi general.

NOTE

• Other folk dances of Gujarat: Garba, Dandiya Raas, Tippani, Padhar, Bhavai and Hudo.

question: Which of the following locations experiences the lowest amount of rainfall during the monsoon season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Leh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Leh (in Ladakh) receives the lowest rainfall among the given places — barely about 10 cm (100 mm) a year. (लेह — सबसे कम वर्षा)

◦ Leh lies in the rain-shadow area on the leeward side of the Great Himalayas; the monsoon winds lose almost all their moisture before crossing the high ranges, making Ladakh a cold desert.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kerala is the first Indian state to receive the South-West Monsoon (around 1 June) and gets very heavy rainfall from the Arabian Sea branch striking the Western Ghats.

• Assam and Meghalaya receive extremely heavy rain from the Bay of Bengal branch funnelled by the Khasi and Garo hills.

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra) in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth (about 1,100+ cm per year).

NOTE

• India's rainfall extremes: Mawsynram (Meghalaya) — highest; Jaisalmer (Rajasthan)/Leh (Ladakh) — lowest.

• Rain shadow examples in India: Leh/Ladakh, the Deccan plateau east of the Western Ghats (e.g., Pune, Solapur).

question: In which of the following cities was the 2023 IPL final match held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final of the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2023 (the 16th edition) was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Motera, Ahmedabad (Gujarat). (आईपीएल 2023 फाइनल — अहमदाबाद)

◦ Chennai Super Kings (CSK) beat Gujarat Titans in a rain-affected final to lift their fifth IPL title, equalling Mumbai Indians' record.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Narendra Modi Stadium is the largest cricket stadium in the world, with a capacity of about 1,32,000 spectators.

• IPL 2023 awards: Shubman Gill — Orange Cap (890 runs); Mohammed Shami — Purple Cap (28 wickets).

• The IPL was started in 2008 by the BCCI; the first title was won by the Rajasthan Royals under Shane Warne.

NOTE

• Most IPL titles: Mumbai Indians and Chennai Super Kings (5 each, as of 2023).

• The 2023 ICC ODI World Cup final was also held at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad (Australia beat India).

question: Who among the following was the director of Kathak Kendra and also opened his own dance school named ‘Kalashram’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Birju Maharaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (1938–2022), the doyen of the Lucknow "Kalka-Bindadin" gharana of Kathak, headed the Kathak Kendra (National Institute of Kathak Dance, New Delhi) as its director, and after retiring in 1998 he founded his own dance school "Kalashram" in Delhi. (पंडित बिरजू महाराज — कलाश्रम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• He was the son and disciple of Pandit Achchan Maharaj, and was also trained by his uncles Pandit Shambhu Maharaj and Pandit Lachhu Maharaj.

• Honours: Padma Vibhushan (1986), Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, Kalidas Samman, and a National Film Award for Best Choreography for the film *Vishwaroopam*.

• He choreographed famous film sequences such as "Kaahe Chhed Mohe" (*Devdas*), "Unnai Kaanadhu Naan" (*Vishwaroopam*) and songs in *Bajirao Mastani* and *Umrao Jaan*.

NOTE

• Kathak is the only classical dance of India with strong Hindu–Muslim (Persian) fusion, developed in the courts of Awadh under Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.

• Kathak gharanas: Lucknow (expression/abhinaya), Jaipur (footwork/technique) and Banaras.

question: What is a budget deficit?
option_1: The excess of government revenue over expenditure
option_2: The amount of money allocated for defence spending
option_3: The amount of money allocated for social welfare programmes
option_4: The excess of government expenditure over revenue
solution_text:
The correct answer is The excess of government expenditure over revenue.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "budget deficit" arises when the government's total expenditure exceeds its total revenue/receipts in a financial year. (बजट घाटा — व्यय > प्राप्तियाँ)

◦ Budget deficit = Total expenditure − Total receipts.

◦ The opposite situation (revenue exceeding expenditure) is a budget surplus; when the two are equal it is a balanced budget.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

Important types of deficit in the Union Budget:

• Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure − Revenue Receipts.

• Fiscal Deficit = Total Expenditure − Total Receipts (excluding borrowings). It indicates the total borrowing requirement of the government.

• Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit − Interest Payments.

• Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit − Grants for creation of capital assets.

NOTE

• Deficits are usually financed by borrowing (market loans, small savings) or by deficit financing (printing money), which can be inflationary.

• The FRBM Act, 2003 (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) sets targets for reducing the fiscal and revenue deficits.

• The Union Budget is presented under Article 112 (Annual Financial Statement) of the Constitution.

question: What is a revenue expenditure?
option_1: Money spent on day-to-day government operations
option_4: Money spent on construction of roads
solution_text:
The correct answer is Money spent on day-to-day government operations.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Revenue expenditure" is expenditure that neither creates any asset nor reduces any liability of the government. It covers the routine, day-to-day running of government departments and services. (राजस्व व्यय)

◦ Examples: salaries and pensions of employees, interest payments, subsidies, grants, defence maintenance, administrative expenses.

◦ It is recurring in nature and is incurred every year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Capital expenditure, in contrast, creates assets or reduces liabilities — e.g., purchasing assets (Option 3), construction of roads, bridges and buildings (Option 4), and repayment of loans/debt (Option 2).

• Similarly, Revenue receipts (taxes, fees, fines, interest received) do not create liabilities or reduce assets, while Capital receipts (borrowings, disinvestment, recovery of loans) do.

NOTE

• A high revenue deficit means the government is borrowing even to meet its consumption expenditure, which is considered fiscally unhealthy.

• Since 2017-18, the distinction between Plan and Non-Plan expenditure has been discontinued; only the Revenue–Capital classification is used.

question: Which Indian musician won the Grammy award for ‘A Meeting by The River’ with Ry Cooder in 1994?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vishwa Mohan Bhatt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt won the Grammy Award (1994) in the Best World Music Album category for the album "A Meeting by the River", recorded with the American slide guitarist Ry Cooder. (विश्व मोहन भट्ट — ग्रैमी 1994)

◦ He is the inventor of the "Mohan Veena" — a modified archtop guitar with 19 strings that blends the sitar, sarod and guitar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (sitar) won several Grammys, including for *West Meets East* (1967) and *Full Circle: Carnegie Hall 2000*, and received a Lifetime Achievement Grammy and the Bharat Ratna (1999).

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia is a legendary bansuri (flute) maestro, awarded the Padma Vibhushan.

• Ustad Zakir Hussain is a tabla maestro who has won multiple Grammy Awards (including three in 2024) and the Padma Vibhushan.

NOTE

• Vishwa Mohan Bhatt was honoured with the Padma Shri (2002) and the Padma Bhushan (2017).

• Other Indian Grammy winners: Ravi Shankar, Zakir Hussain, A. R. Rahman, Ricky Kej, Shankar Mahadevan, Selvaganesh, Rakesh Chaurasia.

question: The holy mountain ‘Kailash’ is located in which neighbouring country of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mount Kailash (Kailash Parvat) is situated in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China, in the Trans-Himalayan (Kailash) range, at a height of about 6,638 m. (कैलाश पर्वत — तिब्बत, चीन)

◦ It is held sacred by four religions — Hinduism (abode of Lord Shiva), Buddhism (Mount Meru/Demchok), Jainism (Rishabhadeva attained liberation at Ashtapada) and Bon.

◦ Nearby lies Lake Mansarovar, the destination of the famous Kailash Mansarovar Yatra, organised by the Ministry of External Affairs through the Lipulekh (Uttarakhand) and Nathu La (Sikkim) routes.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Four great rivers rise near Mount Kailash: the Indus (Sindhu), Sutlej, Brahmaputra (Yarlung Tsangpo) and Karnali (a Ganga tributary).

• Mount Kailash has never been officially climbed, out of respect for its religious sanctity.

NOTE

• India shares land borders with seven countries: Bangladesh (longest), China, Pakistan, Nepal, Myanmar, Bhutan and Afghanistan.

• The India–China border is called the Line of Actual Control (LAC), about 3,488 km long, and it touches Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.

question: In which of the following states of India the ‘Loo’ wind does NOT blow during the summer season?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Goa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Loo" is a strong, hot and dry wind that blows during the summer months (May–June) over the northern plains of India — chiefly Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar. (लू — गर्म शुष्क पवन)

◦ Goa, being a coastal state on the western coast with a maritime (moderating) climate and high humidity from the Arabian Sea, does NOT experience the Loo.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Direct exposure to the Loo can cause heat stroke (sunstroke/lू lagna); temperatures may cross 45 °C.

• Coastal areas have a small annual range of temperature because of the moderating influence of the sea (land and sea breezes), while interior/continental areas have extremes.

NOTE

• Other local winds of India: Kalbaisakhi/Nor'westers (West Bengal, pre-monsoon thunderstorms), Bardoichila (Assam), Mango showers (Kerala/Karnataka), Blossom showers (coffee regions of Karnataka) and Aandhi (dust storms of north-west India).

question:
The Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 seeks to implement the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES). Which of the following statements is correct about CITES?

1. CITES is an agreement between governments to ensure that international trade in the specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of the species.
2. Under CITES, plant and animal specimens are classified into five categories based on the threat to their extinction.
3. The Convention requires countries to regulate the trade of all listed specimens through permits.
4. It also seeks to regulate the possession of live animal specimens.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 3 and 4.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is correct: CITES (Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora) is an agreement between governments to ensure that international trade in specimens of wild animals and plants does not threaten the survival of the species. (साइटिस)

• Statement 2 is INCORRECT: under CITES, specimens are classified into three appendices (Appendix I, II and III) — not five categories.

◦ Appendix I — species threatened with extinction; trade permitted only in exceptional circumstances.

◦ Appendix II — species not necessarily threatened now, but trade must be controlled.

◦ Appendix III — species protected in at least one country that has asked other parties for help in controlling trade.

• Statement 3 is correct: the Convention requires member countries to regulate trade in all listed specimens through permits/certificates.

• Statement 4 is correct: the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022 also regulates the possession of live animal specimens of scheduled species (owners must report and obtain a registration certificate).

Therefore, the correct combination is 1, 3 and 4, i.e. Option 2.

Additional Information

• CITES came into force in 1975; it was drafted after a resolution of the IUCN (1963) and its secretariat is administered by UNEP at Geneva, Switzerland. India joined CITES in 1976.

• The Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 is India's principal wildlife law; the 2022 Amendment rationalised the schedules from six to four (Schedule I & II — animals, Schedule III — plants, Schedule IV — CITES-listed species).

NOTE

• Other environmental conventions: CBD (Rio, 1992), Ramsar (1971, wetlands), Bonn/CMS (migratory species), Basel (hazardous waste), Montreal Protocol (ozone) and the UNFCCC/Paris Agreement (climate).

question: ‘My Story’ is the autobiography of which female writer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kamala Das.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "My Story" (*Ente Katha* in Malayalam, 1973) is the bold and controversial autobiography of Kamala Das, one of India's foremost English and Malayalam writers. (माई स्टोरी — कमला दास)

◦ She wrote poetry in English under the name Kamala Das and fiction in Malayalam under the pen name "Madhavikutty"; after converting to Islam in 1999 she was known as Kamala Surayya.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Her notable poetry collections: *Summer in Calcutta*, *The Descendants*, *The Old Playhouse and Other Poems*. She won the Sahitya Akademi Award (1985) for her English poetry.

• Amrita Pritam — Punjabi poet-novelist, author of *Pinjar* and the poem "Ajj Aakhaan Waris Shah Nu"; her autobiography is "Raseedi Ticket" (Revenue Stamp). She received the Jnanpith (1981) and Padma Vibhushan.

• Pratibha Ray — Odia writer, author of *Yajnaseni*, winner of the Jnanpith Award (2011).

• Ashapurna Devi — Bengali writer, famous for the trilogy *Pratham Pratisruti*, *Subarnalata* and *Bakul Katha*; winner of the Jnanpith (1976).

NOTE

• Famous Indian autobiographies: *The Story of My Experiments with Truth* (Mahatma Gandhi), *An Autobiography/Toward Freedom* (Jawaharlal Nehru), *Wings of Fire* (A. P. J. Abdul Kalam), *Playing It My Way* (Sachin Tendulkar).

question: Which age group of the population are covered under the Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY) scheme of the Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15 to 35 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)" covers poor rural youth in the age group of 15 to 35 years. (डीडीयू-जीकेवाई — 15 से 35 वर्ष)

◦ For vulnerable groups — women, Persons with Disabilities (PwD), Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) and transgender persons — the upper age limit is relaxed to 45 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• DDU-GKY was launched on 25 September 2014 (the birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya) by the Ministry of Rural Development.

• It is the placement-linked skill development component of the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM/Aajeevika) and guarantees placement to at least 70% of trained candidates.

• It is a centrally sponsored scheme, with funding shared between the Centre and States.

NOTE

• Other skilling schemes: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY, 2015), Skill India Mission (2015), Rozgar Mela, Startup Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP) and the National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC).

question: Who was the founder of Naujawan Bharat Sabha?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhagat Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Naujawan Bharat Sabha" was founded in March 1926 at Lahore by Bhagat Singh, along with associates such as Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Yashpal and Sukhdev. (नौजवान भारत सभा — भगत सिंह, 1926)

◦ It was an open, secular, revolutionary youth organisation that aimed to mobilise workers, peasants and youth against British rule and to build a complete independence (Purna Swaraj) movement based on socialist ideas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Bhagat Singh was also a leading member of the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA, 1928), formed under Chandra Shekhar Azad.

• He and Batukeshwar Dutt threw a bomb in the Central Legislative Assembly (8 April 1929) "to make the deaf hear", and courted arrest.

• Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were hanged on 23 March 1931 in the Lahore Conspiracy Case (the killing of J. P. Saunders, avenging the death of Lala Lajpat Rai in the Simon Commission lathi charge). 23 March is observed as Shaheed Diwas.

NOTE

• Bhagat Singh's famous writings: "Why I am an Atheist" and the journal contributions under the pen name Balwant Singh.

• Sardar Ajit Singh (his uncle) led the Pagdi Sambhal Jatta movement (1907) against the Punjab land laws.

question: Which gland gets enlarged in the goitre due to which there is a swelling in the front part of the throat?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Thyroid gland.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Goitre is the abnormal enlargement of the thyroid gland, which lies in the front of the neck (throat), producing a visible swelling. (घेंघा रोग — थायरॉइड ग्रंथि)

◦ Its most common cause is a deficiency of iodine in the diet, which prevents the gland from making enough thyroxine (T₄) and triiodothyronine (T₃), so it enlarges to compensate.

◦ Prevention: use of iodised salt; India runs the National Iodine Deficiency Disorders Control Programme (NIDDCP).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Adrenal gland (on top of the kidneys) — secretes adrenaline (the "emergency/fight-or-flight" hormone), cortisol and aldosterone.

• Pineal gland (in the brain) — secretes melatonin, which regulates the sleep–wake cycle.

• Pituitary gland — the "master gland", secreting growth hormone (GH), TSH, ACTH, FSH, LH, prolactin and oxytocin/ADH (via the posterior lobe).

NOTE

• Thyroid disorders: hypothyroidism (less thyroxine — causes cretinism in children and myxoedema in adults) and hyperthyroidism (excess thyroxine — Graves' disease, exophthalmic goitre).

• The thyroid is the largest endocrine gland in the human body.

question: In which state is the Bhitari temple situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Bhitari temple and the famous Bhitari stone pillar are located at Bhitari village in the Ghazipur district of Uttar Pradesh. (भितरी — गाजीपुर, उत्तर प्रदेश)

◦ The site is protected by the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and contains the remains of a Gupta-period brick temple, a stupa and a monastery.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Bhitari Pillar Inscription of Skandagupta is a key source of Gupta history: it records Skandagupta's victory over the Pushyamitras and the Hunas and mentions the temple/idol of Sarangin (Vishnu) installed by him.

• Other important Gupta-era inscriptions: the Allahabad (Prayag) Prashasti of Samudragupta, composed by Harisena; the Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription of Chandra; the Junagadh (Girnar) inscription of Skandagupta (repair of the Sudarshana Lake).

NOTE

• Gupta period (c. 320–550 CE) is called the "Golden Age of India" for its achievements in art, literature (Kalidasa), mathematics (Aryabhata) and science (Varahamihira).

question: Shubman Gill was in the news for creating a record in his sport. What sport does he play?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shubman Gill is an Indian cricketer — a right-handed top-order batsman from Fazilka, Punjab. (शुभमन गिल — क्रिकेट)

◦ In 2023 he was in the news for a series of records: he became the youngest Indian to score an ODI double century (208 vs New Zealand, Hyderabad, Jan 2023), scored centuries in all three formats in the same year, won the IPL 2023 Orange Cap (890 runs for Gujarat Titans), and was named ICC Men's ODI Cricketer of the Year 2023.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Cricket in India is governed by the BCCI (Board of Control for Cricket in India, founded 1928); internationally by the ICC (International Cricket Council), headquartered at Dubai.

• India won the ICC Cricket World Cup in 1983 and 2011, the T20 World Cup in 2007 and the Champions Trophy in 2002 (shared) and 2013.

NOTE

• Cricket terms: yorker, googly, bouncer, hat-trick, LBW, maiden over, silly point, duck, follow-on.

• Major Indian cricket awards: Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna, Arjuna Award, BCCI's Col. C. K. Nayudu Lifetime Achievement Award.

question: Which of the following does NOT come under Fundamental Duties?
solution_text:
The correct answer is To pay taxes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To pay taxes" is NOT included among the Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A of the Constitution. (कर चुकाना — मौलिक कर्तव्य नहीं है)

◦ The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) had recommended including "to pay taxes" as a fundamental duty, but this recommendation was not accepted by the government while enacting the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) — originally 10, now 11 (the 11th, on providing education to children aged 6–14, was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002) — include:

◦ To abide by the Constitution and respect the National Flag and the National Anthem (Option 4).

◦ To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood (Option 3).

◦ To develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform (Option 1).

◦ To protect the environment, safeguard public property, abjure violence, cherish the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, defend the country, value the composite culture and strive towards excellence.

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

• They are non-justiciable — they cannot be enforced by the courts, unlike Fundamental Rights (Part III).

question: Who among the following was a world famous ‘Sitar’ player?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Ravi Shankar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (1920–2012) was the world's most famous sitar player, who popularised Indian classical music across the globe. (पंडित रवि शंकर — सितार)

◦ He was a disciple of Ustad Allauddin Khan of the Maihar gharana; he taught the sitar to George Harrison of The Beatles and collaborated with the violinist Yehudi Menuhin (*West Meets East*).

◦ He was awarded the Bharat Ratna (1999), the Padma Vibhushan, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and multiple Grammy Awards. He composed the music for *Pather Panchali* and the song *Sare Jahan Se Achha* tune arrangement.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Ustad Shafaat Ahmed Khan was a renowned tabla player of the Delhi gharana.

• Rajaratanam Pillai (T. N. Rajarathinam Pillai) was a legendary nadaswaram player of Carnatic music.

• Ali Ahmad Hussain (Khan) was a celebrated shehnai exponent.

NOTE

• Famous Indian instrumentalists: Sitar — Ravi Shankar, Vilayat Khan, Nikhil Banerjee, Anoushka Shankar; Sarod — Ali Akbar Khan, Amjad Ali Khan; Shehnai — Bismillah Khan; Flute — Hariprasad Chaurasia; Santoor — Shivkumar Sharma; Tabla — Zakir Hussain, Alla Rakha; Violin — L. Subramaniam.

question: Which of the following institutions bagged the maximum medals at the third edition of Khelo India University Games?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Panjab University.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Panjab University, Chandigarh topped the medal tally at the third edition of the Khelo India University Games (KIUG 2022, held in Uttar Pradesh in May–June 2023), bagging the maximum number of medals (26 medals — 21 gold, 4 silver, 1 bronze). (पंजाब विश्वविद्यालय — खेलो इंडिया यूनिवर्सिटी गेम्स)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Previous KIUG champions: Panjab University also topped the 1st edition (2020, Odisha); Jain University, Bengaluru topped the 2nd edition (2021, Karnataka).

• The 3rd KIUG was hosted by Uttar Pradesh across Lucknow, Varanasi, Gorakhpur and Gautam Buddha Nagar, with the finals at Varanasi.

NOTE

• The Khelo India programme was launched in 2018 by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports to revive sports culture at the grassroots.

• Its components: Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG), Khelo India University Games (KIUG), Khelo India Winter Games and Khelo India Para Games.

question: In which year did the All-India Muslim League move a resolution demanding ‘Independent States’ for Muslims in the north-western and eastern areas of the country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1940.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 1940, at its Lahore session (22–24 March 1940), the All-India Muslim League moved the famous resolution demanding "Independent States" for Muslims in the north-western and eastern zones of India. (लाहौर प्रस्ताव / पाकिस्तान प्रस्ताव — 1940)

◦ The session was presided over by Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and the resolution was moved by A. K. Fazlul Haq of Bengal.

◦ It is popularly called the "Pakistan Resolution" (or Lahore Resolution), though the word "Pakistan" did not appear in its text.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The All-India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at Dhaka by Nawab Salimullah Khan, Aga Khan and others.

• Jinnah's Two-Nation Theory held that Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations. The name "Pakistan" had been coined by Chaudhary Rahmat Ali in his 1933 pamphlet *Now or Never*.

• The Muslim League observed 16 August 1946 as "Direct Action Day", which led to the Great Calcutta Killings.

NOTE

• Timeline of related events: Lucknow Pact (1916) — Congress–League unity; Communal Award (1932); Lahore Resolution (1940); August Offer (1940); Cripps Mission (1942); Cabinet Mission (1946); Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947) and the Indian Independence Act, 1947.
